title: Choose the shell composition
question: The roll assigned Column. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Column
options.lineage: one vertical instrument, read top to bottom
options.thesis: Control and notifications live in a single right-edge column so status is always in one place instead of scattered across the screen.
options.viewport: A detached top bar for workspaces, title, clock and power, with a 384px column on the right edge holding sound, display, connectivity and a ranked notification list in one scroll.
options.risk: A tall column on a short screen leaves the notification list cramped.

options.label: Shelf
options.lineage: one horizontal instrument along the bottom edge
options.thesis: The entire shell is a single bar along the bottom edge and every panel grows out of it, so the desktop above stays completely clear.
options.viewport: A 64px shelf at the bottom edge carrying workspaces, running apps, clock and status, with quick settings, a notification card and the launcher search rising out of it.
options.risk: Growing three panels out of one shelf crowds the lower third of the screen.

options.label: Islands
options.lineage: independent floating capsules over an untouched desktop
options.thesis: Each concern is its own small capsule — clock, now playing, workspaces, system, launcher — floating free so the wallpaper stays visible between them.
options.viewport: A clock capsule and now-playing capsule at top centre, a workspace strip on the left edge, a system stack on the right edge, and the launcher as a wide grid across the bottom.
options.risk: Five separate floating pieces read as scattered rather than as one shell.
